conditions.description: replace_preferences deletes the current preferences before the replacement insert without an enclosing transaction, so an insert failure can permanently lose prior data.
conditions.rationale: The destructive write is committed independently from the replacement write in the shown code path.

conditions.description: An insert exception is converted into an ok=true response even though the replacement failed.
conditions.rationale: Returning success hides a failed write and can cause callers to stop retrying or auditing the loss.

conditions.description: The SQL statements shown use positional parameters for user-controlled values and are a negative SQL-injection control.
conditions.rationale: The presence of SQL text alone is not evidence of injection when values are parameterized.

conditions.description: Whether production backups or point-in-time recovery can restore lost preferences cannot be established from this repository fixture.
conditions.rationale: Backup configuration and restore evidence are operational facts outside the supplied source.

conditions.description: Data-integrity readiness must not be cleared while DATA-001 or DATA-002 remains unresolved or recovery capability is unverified.
conditions.rationale: A successful static scan of unrelated paths cannot establish safe destructive-write behavior.
